## Mechanic Signature

| field | design |
| --- | --- |
| wonder_specific_hook | The golden dome over the Rock makes sovereignty public only when the sponsor can publish access rules that bind guards, jurists, pilgrims, endowment officers, and local communities on the Jerusalem platform. |
| core_interaction_loop | The player opens a custody covenant, chooses the compact that governs gates and pilgrim access, resolves a bounded sanctuary dispute, and accepts a final custody settlement rather than waiting through a generic monthly dedication. |
| player_decision_pattern | Choices trade visible sovereignty, tolerant access, guard discipline, and diplomatic witnesses; failure pressure comes from pilgrim rejection or military overreach rather than from elapsed time. |
| state_feedback_model | The incident log records the compact and dispute outcome while the checklist records whether access groups and custody duties have recognized the covenant. |
| failure_or_tension_model | Overbearing guards or rejected witnesses send the rite back to a calmer compact or a reduced proclamation that preserves order but loses diplomatic reach. |
| reward_expression | The reward expresses lawful custody through tolerance of the state faith and diplomatic reputation, with a local memory for protected platform access. |
| reuse_risk_mitigation | This loop depends on the Rock, Jerusalem gates, intercommunal access, and visible custody; a generic sky-dome temple cannot reuse it without losing the contested sanctuary sovereignty proof. |
| custom_archetype_statement | Dome of the Rock needs a bespoke sanctuary compact shape because the decisive state is not a route, actor, stockpile, listener, or five-node incident gauntlet. The four public beats preserve access-group acceptance, custody-duty entrustment, bounded religious opposition, guard overreach, witnessed tolerance, and Jerusalem fixed-site evidence as coupled covenant rows before final reward handoff. |

## Cadence Signature

| field | design |
| --- | --- |
| cadence_type | event_driven |
| cadence_rationale | Event-driven pacing fits because the decisive act is a public covenant and its follow-up dispute, not a progress bar; each event changes who accepts custody of the sanctuary. |
| player_agency_model | The player chooses the access compact, decides how to answer opposition, and determines whether sovereignty is shown as guarded tolerance or narrower control. |
| non_monthly_triggers_or_reason | Non-monthly validation is the visible compact choice and the settlement event that resolves pilgrim, guard, and witness acceptance before reward handoff. |
| pacing_failure_mode | The pacing fails if the covenant becomes flavor over a standard event chain, so the tracked access groups and risk branches remain in design_ir even though the projection compresses them. |
